h: Dull, Wade and the Heart of Highland Perthshire
p: Here's a fact to win you the car quiz on the way up: the tiny village of Dull, right by Aberfeldy, is officially paired with Boring in Oregon and Bland in Australia. The signs make a cracking photo, and it's a nice daft moment before you get into the serious business of antlers and Land Rovers. It also tells you how close you are to proper rural Scotland, with farms, woodland and big hills in every direction.

To get the most from a safari, ask questions. The guides know this landscape inside out, and kids who quiz them about what deer eat in winter, why stags roar in autumn or how to read tracks on the hill tend to come home buzzing with facts. A small pair of binoculars each saves squabbling, and a phone with a decent zoom will thank you when something appears on a far ridge. Motion sickness can catch out the odd passenger on rough tracks, so anyone prone to it should sit up front if possible and skip the heavy breakfast.

Back in Aberfeldy, look out for Wade's Bridge across the Tay, built in the 1730s by General George Wade as part of his military roads and still carrying traffic today. Beside it stands the Black Watch memorial, marking the spot where the famous regiment was first mustered. Grown-ups might fancy a dram at the Aberfeldy distillery, home of Dewar's, while Castle Menzies at nearby Weem is a striking old tower house. Head a few miles west to Fortingall and you'll find an ancient yew in the churchyard that's reckoned to be thousands of years old.
